description: Cockpit section only of the only aircraft in the world shot down in air-to-air combat by accident: hit by a missile fired in error during air combat training on 22 Nov 1995; the pilot ejected and survived; the wreck was raised investigated and sold for scrap and part of it was acquired here

Nose section with red paint traces in the car park; the radio call plate in the cockpit confirms 46-8571; struck off 29 Aug 1968 and used from about 1970 as a skeleton instructional airframe at the Hamamatsu 1st Technical School which is why panels are missing
Nose section propped against a building; the radio call plate has been removed with the panel so identity rests on a 2013 photograph of the adjoining rear cockpit section marked 697
A further F-104J section held on the site
Outdoors since at least January 2004 when JA7352 was painted on the underside
Present since at least the end of 2007
Second R22 present since about 2014; no registration established
Third R22 present since about 2014; no registration established
Nose section only; internationally known as the only F-15 nose anywhere from an airframe destroyed in an air-to-air engagement; displayed outdoors as an eye-catcher
